title: Nimbus Health - Redwood Console: Tracing & Request Logs Debugging Walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Nimbus Health through Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Focus on debugging latency spikes and error regressions for their private deployment candidate. Key asks: SOC 2 evidence, private VPC networking constraints, ability to export full request logs, and a benchmark run on a synthetic workload. Agreed next steps: send SOC2 + security pack, schedule a benchmark call, and share runbook template.
next_steps: Maya to send SOC 2 and security pack by 2027-09-27
Luca to schedule benchmark run with Nimbus scripted workload (target: 2027-10-01)
Sofia to provide sample traffic profile and high-latency request IDs by 2027-09-29
Priya to share runbook and steps for tracing-based RCA template by 2027-09-28
action_items: Luca: Prepare benchmark environment and invite Nimbus to test run (due 2027-10-01)
Sofia: Send sample request IDs and traffic pattern CSV (due 2027-09-29)
Priya: Draft runbook for tracing -> request-log correlation (due 2027-09-28)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-09-24
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Solutions Eng), Ethan (CTO - Nimbus), Sofia (Lead ML Eng), Daniel (DevOps)
---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Ethan: Ethan here.
[00:07] Sofia: Sofia here.
[00:09] Daniel: Daniel, present.
[00:12] Maya: Cool. Luca, do you wanna kick off with the tracing overview?
[00:17] Luca: Yeah sure, thanks. So we'll jump into the Redwood Console, specifically the tracing tab, error analysis and how you can correlate that to request logs. Apologies if the screen share lags a bit.
[00:28] Luca: First thing, tracing shows per-request spans: model variant used, routing decision (hosted/dedicated/private), latency breakdown per-stage - tokenizer, model, post-process. The timeline is interactive so you can zoom into hot spans.
[00:40] Sofia: Can we filter by customer-id or by model version? We have multiple pinned variants for A/B testing.
[00:44] Luca: Yep, you can filter by model version tag, route, and also by metadata like customer_id. There's also a queryable field to surface only requests routed to dedicated pools - useful for your Dedicated pilot.
[00:55] Daniel: Is the KV cache breakdown visible? We saw a lot of prefix cache misses in our metrics.
[00:59] Luca: Good question. We show cache hit/miss rates per-request and aggregate. In the trace detail you can see KV lookups and whether the fallback to full decode occurred. Note transcription: "kay vee cache" sometimes shows up in logs as KV-cash in older traces - there was a historical tag mismatch, we've cleaned most of it but older traces can be noisy.
[01:19] Ethan: In some of our spikes we saw model time jump from 120ms to 900ms, any quick idea how tracing helps root cause that?
[01:24] Luca: You can expand model-stage spans to see token generation distributions and check whether the kernel selection changed (fp32 -> int8 degrade) or if there was model variant fallback. Also check scheduling waits - when dedicated pool is saturated, requests may queue which shows up as schedule wait.
[01:38] Sofia: About fallback, if a route fails to get capacity, does Redwood automatically route to hosted? We need deterministic behavior for latency-sensitive features.
[01:45] Priya: We have routing policies - you can set strict route (fail) or allow fallback to compatible variants or hosted. We recommend setting a canary/fallback policy for non-blocking flows. For your latency-critical calls you can set strict and an SLA alert.
[02:00] Daniel: Where are the request logs stored? For auditing we need raw request/response payloads for 90 days in our region.
[02:07] Maya: By default request logs are kept for 30 days; for enterprise we support custom retention and region-based storage. We can provide an export to your S3 bucket or a secure log forwarder. We'll send the exact retention SLAs in the security pack.
[02:20] Sofia: Can we get full token-level logs? We want to reproduce stochastic outputs for debug.
[02:24] Luca: We support token-level logs but they're treated as PII-sensitive in some cases so access is gated. You can enable detailed logging at route-level and then logs are shipped to your configured storage. There's a cost and privacy note - we'll include that in the docs.
[02:40] Ethan: On compliance, we need SOC 2 plus encryption-at-rest with our KMS. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[02:46] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations for key management and we can do Bring-Your-Own-Key. SOC 2 Type II report is part of the security pack I'll share.
[02:58] Sofia: Back to debugging, how do we go from a trace to the actual request log? We sometimes see an error in trace but can't find the request in our logs.
[03:04] Luca: Each trace attaches a request_id. In the request logs UI you can search by request_id, session_id, or time-range. The trace view has a direct link "Open request log" which jumps you to the full payload and any downstream shading (transformers pipeline steps).
[03:18] Daniel: There was one mention last time about "prefix caching" mis-tagging causing wrong KV hits. Is there a way to surface anomalies in cache behavior?
[03:25] Priya: We have an anomaly detector you can enable that raises alerts on cache hit-rate regressions beyond a threshold. It also ties back to the tracing timeline so you can see where hit-rate dropped and which keys were affected.
[03:36] Sofia: Great. Can we see a quick demo of diagnosing a high-latency request?
[03:40] Luca: Sure, I'll pull up a sample trace. (screen share) Here's a request at 14:02 that hit a 720ms model stage. Expand timeline - you can see scheduling wait was 480ms, model stage 200ms, tokenizer 20ms. So the bulk was scheduling. Click the scheduling span to see pool saturation metrics.
[04:02] Luca: You can see this pool had high concurrent requests and an autoscale event delayed. That points to either incorrect autoscale config or a burst above configured burst capacity.
[04:14] Ethan: For autoscale, we set min=2, max=6, target_cpu=70% - what's Redwood's recommendation for text-gen workloads?
[04:21] Priya: For generation bursts we recommend setting higher burst capacity and more aggressive scale-up triggers, because cold-starts and kernel swaps can add 200-500ms. Also use prefix/KV caching to reduce model work if your requests share context.
[04:36] Sofia: We use a lot of dynamic context; KVs are tricky. If prefix cache is missed frequently could that explain the sporadic higher token counts?
[04:42] Luca: Yes, misses force full decode; you'll see token counts and downstream model time increase. We can correlate cache-miss events across traces to see if a particular client pattern is causing the misses.
[04:55] Daniel: Regarding request logs export - can we stream to our SIEM? We use Splunk.
[05:00] Maya: Yes we have log forwarders; Splunk, Datadog, S3, GCS. For real-time streaming to SIEM we can set up an event webhook or Kinesis stream. We'll include integration notes.
[05:12] Ethan: A non-technical ask: if we do Private deployment on-prem, can we still use the Console for tracing or is that self-hosted too?
[05:20] Maya: Private has two modes: hosted control plane with private data plane (Console hosted but data never leaves your VPC) or fully on-prem console. Most customers choose hosted control plane for ease but we can accommodate air-gapped. We'll put options in the proposal.
[05:36] Sofia: Let's pivot to an actual error we saw - 500s with "decode failure" in logs.
[05:40] Luca: Show me an example request id?
[05:42] Sofia: Here's one: req_20270923_9a3f7.
[05:45] Luca: Searching... (typing) Found it. Trace shows model stage failed at token 87 with a decode error. Expand the error span - it includes stack snippet and kernel fallback. Looks like model variant attempted an int8 kernel that had an unsupported op - it fell back to CPU for that token causing a spike and eventual OOM on the worker.
[06:07] Priya: We also track error fingerprints in the error analysis view so repeated decode failures get grouped and you can see upstream: which model binary, which kernel, which hardware.
[06:18] Sofia: Can we exclude specific kernel variants or mark certain model builds as non-fallback?
[06:22] Luca: You can pin a model build and disable automatic kernel substitution, though that increases risk of OOMs. For production we suggest pinned builds with careful rollout and canary testing.
[06:34] Daniel: For the OOMs, how do we get logs from the worker?
[06:37] Luca: The request log includes worker stderr snippets and process metrics. For full debug we can give you a worker-level archive on request for the bench run. It's gated to engineers with appropriate role.
[06:48] Ethan: That leads to RBAC and SSO - we need SAML + SCIM, and only certain roles can see token-level logs.
[06:55] Maya: Supported. Role-based access and audit logs are part of the enterprise bundle. We log who accessed what and when.
[07:05] Sofia: Do we get programmatic access to traces and logs? We prefer CI-driven assertions.
[07:09] Luca: Yes we expose APIs to query traces and request logs; there's pagination and filters. We'll share API examples.
[07:18] Maya: Quick question - any blockers to running a benchmark?
[07:21] Sofia: Network constraints: our VPC has strict egress rules. We'll need a peering or VPN so Redwood can run the synthetic load against our Private deployment. Also timeline: we'd prefer to run next week.
[07:33] Priya: We can do peering or a temporary test tunnel. For the synthetic workload we'll need traffic profile and a list of model versions.
[07:42] Luca: For the benchmark we'll instrument tracing and collect request logs; we typically run a 30-minute ramp and capture tail latency. Also we'll run a few fault-injection scenarios to validate fallbacks.
[07:54] Daniel: Fault injection sounds useful. Can you simulate model variant failure?
[07:57] Luca: Yes we can mark variants as unhealthy or throttle pools to force fallback. That helps validate canary policies.
[08:05] Ethan: Ok. Any questions about pricing for detailed logs and longer retention?
[08:10] Maya: There's a retention/add-on charge for extended logs and for token-level retention. We'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[08:18] Sofia: One more technical: is trace sampling adjustable? We need to avoid excessive volume in production.
[08:23] Priya: Sampling is configurable per-route - you can set deterministic sampling for error traces and lower sampling for success traces. We also support adaptive sampling to increase capture when anomalies are detected.
[08:36] Maya: Let's do a quick recap of agreed items and next steps. Luca?
[08:40] Luca: Recap: We'll run benchmark next week, enable detailed tracing for the benchmark, collect request logs and share diagnostics. We'll also triage the decode-failure group and propose mitigations (pin builds, disable kernel fallback).
[08:52] Maya: I'll send SOC2 and security docs, and a proposal with retention/pricing. Priya will share runbook. Sofia to send traffic profile.
[09:02] Ethan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:05] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email - meeting end.
---
Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings on acronyms (KMS sometimes transcribed as K-M-S, KV as kay vee), minor overlaps and filler words.
